10.1109/ectc51846.2026.00049.abstract: Lifetime and reliability are crucial performance indicators for electronics especially in the fields of automotive, avionics and industrial electronics. Mechanical test procedures are key methods to assess lifetime and reliability which typically include several vibration test methods and drop or shock testing. Shock testing using shaker equipment is a relatively new topic which enables combined load scenarios. Previous works proposed a test vehicle which enabled efficient failure generation [1]. First test results showed a rapid decrease in solder joint reliability at raised temperatures. The test vehicle design was adapted for testing of QFN48 and leadless chip resistor (LCR0603) components in addition to the custom Flip-Chip (FC) components. Lifetime testing at board level using shock loads with 130 G amplitude and a pulse width of 2 ms was carried out at high temperature of 125 °C. Results clearly identified QFN solder joints as most critical compared to these of both other components. A test vehicle with mixed component types was developed to allow for direct comparison in terms of lifetime between the tested components. As expected, the QFN solder joints were revealed to be the most critical ones. LCRs placed in close proximity to QFN components were found to fail slightly earlier compared to those placed next to FC components. The assumed cause of this is a change in the local deformation behavior of the PCB in close proximity to the QFN and FC components respectively. Which in turn is due to the different stiffening effect of the QFN and FC components as they differ in footprint size, number and arrangement of solder joints as well as effective package stiffness. In-depth analysis by cross sectioning identified weak points in QFN solder joints, which could be mitigated by corner bond or side fill technologies. Both, test method and test vehicles design have proven themselves to examine the temperature dependent shock reliability of different package types.

10.1116/6.0005373.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) is a promising technique for fabricating nanoscale devices. By selectively depositing materials onto specific areas, AS-ALD offers advantages over traditional top-down fabrication techniques such as overcoming alignment limitations and reducing material waste. In order to achieve selectivity, the vapor-phase application of small molecule inhibitors (SMIs) delivers an industrially viable approach. The library of available SMIs that have been tested for AS-ALD is currently limited, and experimental screening of all possible candidates is unfeasible. In addition, the computational screening of SMIs for optimal performance is currently done by the individual analysis of candidate molecules, a process that can be limited based on computational time. To speed up the future screening procedures, this study explores the potential use of descriptor properties in AS-ALD, as a concept borrowed from catalysis. By considering the electronegativity of the core atom of a SMI, we investigated the adsorption behavior of 20 SMI candidates on Al(OH)3, Si(OH)4, Al(NH2)3, and Si(NH2)4 cluster models, representing Al2O3, SiO2, AlN, and Si3N4 surfaces. This work demonstrates the linear correlation between the electronegativity of the core atom and the adsorption energy of the SMI. The dataset also identifies five potential SMI candidates for the inhibition of oxide surfaces and six candidates for the nitride surfaces. This study supports the use of descriptors as a viable methodology for SMI screening.

10.1515/mt-2025-0440.abstract: Abstract The decomposition of ammonia (NH 3 ) presents a viable pathway for hydrogen production, leveraging ammonia’s high hydrogen content and established infrastructure. This study numerically assesses the impact of microchannel reactor geometry on the efficiency of NH 3 decomposition, employing ruthenium-based catalysts. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was developed and validated against experimental data, incorporating the Temkin-Pyzhev kinetic model. The analysis explores various microchannel geometries with different catalyst distribution strategies, including rectangular and semicircular configurations. Results indicate that optimizing channel geometry significantly enhances hydrogen production efficiency while reducing catalyst consumption. The 1.5X (scaled with respect to the base case) thicker configuration achieved a 10 % improvement in conversion per catalyst mass compared to the base case. In contrast, constant catalyst thickness in a 2X-expanded channel demonstrated the lowest conversion efficiency. Additionally, semicircular geometries exhibited lower pressure drops, offering advantages for scaling up hydrogen production. These findings contribute to the design of advanced microreactors for sustainable hydrogen production, highlighting the importance of geometric optimization in enhancing catalytic performance and process efficiency.

10.20517/microstructures.2025.129.abstract: Ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>) plays a crucial role in global agriculture and the development of emerging hydrogen energy systems. However, developing highly efficient catalysts for NH<sub>3</sub> synthesis under mild conditions remains a significant challenge due to kinetic and thermodynamic limitations. In this study, we report a Ru/CeO<sub>2</sub> catalyst synthesized using a metal-organic framework (MOF)-derived strategy, which allows for simultaneous control over the morphology of CeO<sub>2</sub> (nanorod shaped), the concentration of oxygen vacancies, and the dispersion of Ru. The optimized catalyst containing 0.5 wt.% Ru delivered an impressive NH<sub>3</sub> synthesis rate of 4,665 μmol gcat<sup>-1</sup> h<sup>-1</sup> at 400 °C and 50 bar, while maintaining excellent stability for 45 h of continuous operation. In addition, it achieved a high NH<sub>3</sub> conversion of 93% at 550 °C and 1 bar. Notably, its performance surpasses that of conventional Ru-based catalysts by nearly twofold when normalized to the Ru loading. Comprehensive characterizations, including in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and scanning transmission electron microscopy, reveal the formation of abundant oxygen vacancies, sub-nanometer Ru clusters, and strong metal support interaction. These factors collectively enhance the activation of N<sub>2</sub> and its hydrogenation. This study highlights the effectiveness of MOF-templated defect engineering in developing robust Ru/CeO<sub>2</sub> catalysts and provides valuable insights into structure-performance relationships. The dual functionality in both NH<sub>3</sub> synthesis and decomposition highlights the potential of this approach for energy-efficient NH<sub>3</sub>-based energy systems.

10.21203/rs.3.rs-9593284/v1.abstract: Abstract The transition toward the low carbon energy systems has accelerated the interest in the green hydrogen and the ammonia as the sustainable energy carriers. This study presents the design and the performance evaluation of the integrated renewable based system for the hydrogen production through electrolysis and the subsequent conversion to the ammonia. The hybrid solar photovoltaic and wind configuration is modeled in MATLAB and Simulink to supply the power to the proton exchange membrane electrolyzer, followed by the hydrogen storage and the Haber–Bosch synthesis. The objective is to assess the system performance under the variable renewable conditions and to quantify both the technical as well as the economic feasibility. The simulation results indicate that the system produces approximately 48–52 kg/day of hydrogen at the rated electrolyzer capacity of 100 kW, where this supports the ammonia production in the range of 270–300 kg/day, with the conversion efficiency of about 20–21 percent. The overall energy conversion efficiency from the renewable input to the ammonia output is found to be 28–34 percent. The estimated levelized cost of hydrogen ranges between 3.8 and 4.5 USD/kg, while the ammonia production costs vary from 680 to 820 USD/ton. The novelty of this work lies in the integrated dynamic modeling of the renewable variability, coupled with the hydrogen buffering and the techno economic assessment. The proposed framework offers the realistic representation of the system behaviour and provides the insights into improving the feasibility of the green ammonia production systems.

10.2139/ssrn.6714350.abstract: A binary alloy could exist with different arrangements of atoms (disordered or ordered) that are expected to influence their properties differently. For the optimum effect of alloying, ordered phase, especially the B2-ordering in FeCo alloys should be advantageous. However, the synthesis of an ordered phase is challenging, especially due to the relatively similar atomic sizes. Here, we report the successful synthesis of both disordered as well as B2-ordered FeCo alloys and demonstrate their performance in electrocatalytic ammonia synthesis by nitrate reduction (NO3RR). The synthesis involves the pyrolysis followed by natural and rapid cooling. Remarkably, the B2-ordered phase forms with natural cooling that delivers an ammonia yield rate that is over four times higher than its disordered phase, achieving 2.213 ± 0.064 mmol (NH3) h-1 mgcat.-1 and surpassing many state-of-the-art catalysts reported to date. This enhanced activity arises from the atomic-scale ordering enables the optimized electronic structure, which facilitates more effective reactant adsorption and activation. Though we have demonstrated effective ammonia synthesis, we strongly believe that the same can be employed for other catalytic activities and sensing applications where adsorption of different species plays a key role. Finally, as a-proof-of-concept, we have demonstrated NO3RR-based battery using FeCo as cathode catalyst.

10.2139/ssrn.6736737.abstract: Electromagnetic pollution arising from booming communication and radar systems demands lightweight microwave absorbers with strong attenuation, broad effective absorption bandwidth, and desirable impedance matching. Nevertheless, developing sustainable, low-cost, and scalable synthetic routes toward high-performance absorbers remains a challenge. Herein, we report a functional upcycling strategy, in which Fe-rich residues derived from spent LiFePO₄ (SLFP) batteries are adopted as a green iron precursor to fabricate advanced Fe-C microwave absorbers via solvent-free, second-scale flash Joule heating (FJH). The residues were blended with conductive carbon black and subjected to multiple FJH cycles at 90 V to synthesize a series of carbon-supported multiphase Fe-based composites (denoted as C@MFeX). During the FJH process, current focusing generates interfacial hot spots, while ultrafast heating-quenching drives in situ phase transformation and nanoscale anchoring of Fe species. This behavior constructs multiphase Fe components endowed with high-density gradient Fe-C interfacial coupling. Meanwhile, the carbon matrix undergoes graphene-like structural reconstruction with reserved intrinsic defects, forming percolated conductive pathways and abundant heterogeneous interfaces. These unique structural features synergistically facilitate multiple polarization processes and coupled dielectric–magnetic losses, further optimizing microwave attenuation capability and impedance matching. Among all as-prepared samples, C@MFe7 delivers the optimal microwave absorption performance, achieving a minimum reflection loss of −52.25 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.62 GHz at a matching thickness of 1.68 mm. This work demonstrates a rapid and scalable FJH platform for upgrading underutilized SLFP-derived wastes into high-value magneto-dielectric microwave absorbers, providing a feasible and sustainable pathway for high-value functional material fabrication from retired battery resources.

10.2139/ssrn.6759615.abstract: The widespread deployment of renewable energy requires scalable, distributed storage solutions capable of aligning intermittent generation with continuous demand. Green ammonia is a promising energy vector, yet its production relies on the Haber Bosch process, the epitome of industrial economies of scale. This work provides a rigorous, scale-resolved assessment of where conventional ammonia synthesis ceases to be technically and economically viable. A 2-dimensional pseudo-homogeneous packed-bed model is developed to quantify the influence of radial heat losses across production scales. The analysis reveals that the assumption of adiabatic reactor operation, ubiquitous in the literature, fails below 100 tonnes per day, where conductive heat losses become comparable to reaction enthalpy. At intermediate scales, this loss necessitates additional reactor beds, while at very small scales (1 tonne per day), conventional reactor designs fail thermally. To address this, a novel variably insulated reactor concept is introduced, enabling controlled radial heat dissipation to maintain optimal reaction trajectories. This redesign reduces reactor volume and capital cost by 35–65% relative to adiabatic assumptions at scales between 1-50 tonnes per day. In addition, a comprehensive economic evaluation of the whole ammonia production process demonstrates that economies of scale fail below 100 tonnes per day, driven primarily by compression and equipment costs. Even under favourable hydrogen pricing, plants below approximately 50 tonnes per day remain economically infeasible. This study establishes the technical and economic limits of small-scale Haber Bosch synthesis and identifies targeted reactor innovations and alternative low-pressure process routes as essential for realising distributed green ammonia production.

During the reaction, the release of lattice hydrogen from HWO accelerates the nitrogen reduction reaction. Active hydrogen species generated at efficient water-dissociation sites on Ru spill over onto HWO, replenishing the lattice hydrogen and thereby establishing an efficient dynamic hydrogen cycle. Benefitting from the unique mechanism, an excellent NH3 synthesis performance of 228.5 μmol g−1 h−1 is achieved, along with the full-spectrum light utilization. This study not only confirms a new lattice-hydrogen-mediated photocatalytic N2 reduction pathway, but also paves a new way for the rational design of efficient and stable hydrogen tungsten bronze photocatalytic systems.

10.2139/ssrn.6849830.abstract: Ammonia (NH₃) is a promising hydrogen carrier, yet its efficient decomposition to COₓ-free hydrogen remains challenging, especially at low temperatures. Herein, we systematically investigate the influence of calcination atmosphere (air, Ar, and NH₃) on the structure and catalytic performance of Ru/MgO catalysts for NH₃ decomposition. Comprehensive characterizations (XRD, TEM, XPS, H₂-TPR, CO chemisorption, and NH₃-DRIFTS) reveal that the calcination atmosphere critically dictates the chemical state of Ru species, their dispersion, and the metal-support interaction. Calcination in air or Ar leads to the formation of an ultrathin, irreducible RuO₂ overlayer strongly bonded to MgO via interfacial Ru–O–Mg linkages. This RuO₂ overlayer severely suppresses NH₃ activation and N₂ desorption, resulting in poor catalytic activity (NH₃ conversion <30% at 400 °C) with high apparent activation energies (109–149 kJ·mol⁻¹). Strikingly, subsequent re-calcination of these samples in NH₃ fails to convert the RuO₂ overlayer into active metallic Ru, demonstrating its irreversible nature. The resulting Ru/MgO-NH₃ catalyst delivers exceptional performance: >99% NH₃ conversion at 400 ℃, a high H₂ formation rate of 575.0 mmol·g_Ru⁻¹·min⁻¹, and outstanding stability over 100 h. Its turnover frequency (2.12 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹) far exceeds those of air/Ar-calcined counterparts, and its apparent activation energy is as low as 69.8 kJ·mol⁻¹. This work not only establishes NH₃ calcination as a facile and effective strategy to construct highly active metallic Ru⁰ sites, but also uncovers the irreversible formation of a RuO₂ overlayer under non-reductive atmospheres, offering new insights into the rational design of robust Ru-based catalysts for low-temperature ammonia decomposition.

We first evaluated the thermodynamic stability of various Ru-doped SAAs against dopant aggregation and subsurface segregation. We then systematically investigated the reaction energetics of ammonia decomposition, focusing on the trade-off between ammonia dehydrogenation and the associative desorption of N2 and H2. Thermodynamic screening identified Ru/Fe, Ru/Co, and Ru/Ni SAAs as promising candidates with favorable energetics for associative desorption. Notably, further kinetic analysis revealed that Ru/Fe SAA is highly active for ammonia decomposition, exhibiting reduced barriers for both dehydrogenation and associative desorption compared with pure Ru. In addition, we identified the adsorption energy of atomic nitrogen as an effective descriptor correlating well with catalytic reactivity across the SAAs. This work provides fundamental insights into overcoming catalytic limitations through atomic doping strategies, while demonstrating how SAAs maximize the atomic efficiency of scarce noble metals and guiding the design of more efficient catalysts for ammonia decomposition.

Here, we demonstrate a voltage-regulated flash Joule heating strategy that converts commercial V2O5 into kinetically favorable mixed-phase vanadium oxide cathodes within seconds. During the ultrafast electrical pulse, carbon black simultaneously acts as a Joule-heating medium, conductive scaffold and reductive agent, enabling rapid oxygen extraction and voltage-dependent reconstruction of the V2O5 lattice. By tuning the discharge voltage, the reduction degree and phase composition can be precisely modulated: insufficient voltage preserves poorly activated V2O5, whereas excessive voltage causes over-reduction and structural degradation. The optimized FV2O5-140 cathode achieves a balanced V2O5/V2O3 heterophase structure, where mixed-valence vanadium sites, defect-rich local environments and an interconnected porous carbon network synergistically accelerate charge transfer, enhance electrolyte penetration and shorten Zn2+ diffusion pathways. Consequently, FV2O5-140 delivers a reversible capacity of 404 mAh g-1 at 0.2 A g-1, retains 263 mAh g-1 at 5 A g-1, and maintains 172 mAh g-1 after 1000 cycles at 5 A g-1. Ex situ XRD, SEM/EDS and EIS further confirm reversible Zn2+ insertion/extraction, preserved electrode morphology and reduced charge-transfer resistance after activation. 10.26434/chemrxiv.15003821/v1.abstract: Pourbaix diagrams are essential tools for guiding aqueous electrochemical experiments, yet they are often limited to pure metals or alloys and the equilibrium lines in the Pourbaix diagrams are considered to be deterministic phase boundaries despite substantial variation in reported thermodynamic parameters. Here, we present a probabilistic Pourbaix diagram framework that incorporates complexing agents and explicitly accounts for the variability in equilibrium constants, demonstrated through a case study on the aqueous nickel–ammonia–citrate electrolyte system. Monte Carlo simulation (𝑁 = 1000 samples) is used to propagate variability in reported equilibrium constants through a multicomponent speciation model. We find that ammonia progressively stabilises dissolved nickel(II) under alkaline conditions by forming Ni(NH3) n 2+ complexes (𝑛 = 1–6), shifting the Ni(OH) 2 precipitation onset from pH 6.63 (ammonia-free) to pH 12.66 at a 20:1 ammonia-to-nickel molar ratio. Citrate achieves a comparable stabilisation effect at lower concentrations, delaying precipitation to pH 9.29 at a citrate-to-nickel molar ratio of only 2.5. For the combined bath (𝐶 Ni = 0.2, 𝐶 Cit = 0.25, 𝐶 NH3 = 0.33 mol L −1 ), the probabilistic treatment reveals substantial uncertainty in the onset of Ni(OH) 2 (s) precipitation: while the deterministic model predicts a sharp onset near pH 8.9, the Monte Carlo ensemble indicates that precipitation may begin as early as pH 6 and may not become certain until around pH 11 due to uncertainity in the underlying thermodynamic data. The resulting probabilistic Pourbaix diagram identifies domains of high thermodynamic confidence from those of genuine ambiguity, providing a foundation for the design and interpretation of nickel electrodeposition from ammonia–citrate baths.

10.33313/390/045.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding and controlling nitrogen pickup in Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) steelmaking requires a comprehensive evaluation of charge design, gas-metal interaction, slag behavior, and operational stability. This study investigates the multifactorial mechanisms governing nitrogen absorption at EAF, using plant data from heats with varying scrap ratios. The results show a clear relationship between higher scrap content and increased nitrogen before tapping, driven by both the initial nitrogen associated with scrap and operational adjustments such as elevated coke injection to sustain slag foaming. Slag oxidation state, effective viscosity, and foaming index were evaluated. High-scrap heats exhibited higher FeO levels, lower effective viscosity, and reduced foamability, conditions that enhance metal-slag interfacial exposure and promote nitrogen incorporation. Thermodynamic assessments indicate that Ca/Mg nitride formation is unfavorable at typical steelmaking temperatures and oxygen potentials, suggesting that slag is unlikely to serve as a stable nitrogen sink. The combined metallurgical, operational, and thermodynamic evidence demonstrates that nitrogen pickup in EAF production is primarily governed by scrap characteristics, carbon/oxygen practice, early-stage bath exposure, and the dynamic behavior of oxidized, low-viscosity slags.

10.3390/cryst16060359.abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction (eNO3−RR) to NH3 is a sustainable solution. However, it faces challenges like poor selectivity and competitive hydrogen evolution (HER). We report a novel Ga@FeGa3 catalyst for efficient eNO3−RR. Its unique rough, flaky morphology provides abundant active sites. The optimized electron structure enhanced the nitrogen intermediate binding. The catalyst also shows exceptional hydrophilicity. This aids reactant access, rapid product desorption, and suppresses HER. These effects give Ga@FeGa3 outstanding eNO3−RR performance. It achieves an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 97.84% at −1.4 V (vs. Ag/AgCl) and a 3.87 mg h−1 cm−2 yield at −1.5 V. It also maintains high selectivity and stability for over 12 h. This work highlights rational intermetallic design. Such design optimizes active sites, electronic structure, and surface wettability. This is crucial for multi-electron transfer reactions. It offers a general strategy for high-performance electrocatalysts.

10.3390/ma19101919.abstract: A conformal SiNx coating on carbon nanotubes (CNTs) was achieved by combining transient UV–ozone surface functionalization with a two-step atomic layer deposition (ALD) process. UV–ozone treatment gradually increased the defect density of CNTs, with the ID/IG ratio increasing from 0.05 for pristine CNTs to 0.25 after 7 min of exposure, while the overall fibrous CNT network remained intact. However, prolonged UV–ozone exposure beyond 10 min led to a sharp increase in the ID/IG ratio to 0.46, accompanied by structural degradation of the CNT membrane. Hydroxyl (-OH), epoxy (C-O-C), and carbonyl (C=O) groups were introduced by UV–ozone treatment and were partially removed during subsequent high-temperature processing. Accordingly, direct high-temperature ALD resulted in incomplete SiNx coverage of the CNTs, suggesting insufficient nucleation. A two-step ALD process, consisting of several cycles of low-temperature nucleation at 100 °C followed by high-temperature growth at 700 °C, enabled more conformal deposition of SiNx on CNTs. In addition, both annealing and ALD reduced the defect level toward that of pristine CNTs, supporting the transient nature of UV–ozone-induced functionalization.

10.3390/ma19101953.abstract: The electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) represents a promising strategy for wastewater remediation and sustainable ammonia (NH3) production. However, its practical application is hindered by low selectivity and competition from the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, a series of PtBi-CoX (X = 4.9, 5.3, and 6.1) ternary alloy nanoplates was synthesized via a one-pot method with tunable Co content. Structural characterization indicates that Co incorporation does not significantly alter the hexagonal crystal structure of the PtBi phase. Electrochemical measurements reveal that the NO3RR performance varies with PtBi-CoX (X = 4.9, 5.3, 6.1), with PtBi-Co5.3 exhibiting the optimal balance of activity and selectivity among the studied samples. At −0.5 V vs. RHE, it achieves a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 97.75 ± 0.75% and an NH3 yield rate of 9.33 ± 0.50 mg h−1 mgcat−1 under the tested conditions. In addition, the catalyst exhibits relatively suppressed HER activity compared to samples with higher Co content, along with good stability. These findings provide useful insights into the design of PtBi-based ternary alloy catalysts for efficient nitrate reduction.

10.3390/molecules31111805.abstract: Ammonia is a key chemical for fertilizers, industrial processes, and emerging energy applications, yet its conventional production via the Haber–Bosch process is associated with high energy demand and significant greenhouse gas emissions. In this context, electrochemical routes for ammonia synthesis have attracted increasing attention as a potential sustainable alternative, enabling nitrogen conversion under milder conditions and using renewable electricity. This review examines recent advances in electrochemical ammonia production, focusing on nitrogen reduction mechanisms, catalyst development, and electrochemical system design. The main reaction pathways for nitrogen activation are analyzed, together with the role of electrocatalysts in determining activity and selectivity. Progress in catalyst engineering, electrolyte optimization, and reactor configuration is discussed, with particular emphasis on strategies to mitigate competing reactions such as hydrogen evolution. In addition, alternative approaches based on nitrate reduction are considered due to their promising performance and potential integration with wastewater treatment. Unlike many recent reviews primarily focused on catalyst development or individual reaction pathways, this review provides an integrated perspective encompassing nitrogen reduction, nitrate reduction, electrolyte engineering, reactor architectures, and techno-economic considerations, thereby highlighting the interdependence between materials design, reaction environment, and system-level integration for scalable electrochemical ammonia synthesis.

10.3390/pr14101583.abstract: Addressing the challenges of fluctuating renewable energy integration and stable green ammonia production, this study develops and optimizes a deeply integrated system comprising Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC), Liquid Air Energy Storage (LAES), Air Separation Units (ASU), and Haber–Bosch (HB) synthesis. We constructed a simulation model in Aspen Plus incorporating Ru/C catalyst kinetic parameters to analyze key subsystem parameters and optimize operating conditions based on maximized economy and efficiency. At the integrated system level, a parametric analysis of ammonia condensation temperature was further conducted to investigate the coupling characteristics. Using real power output data from Inner Mongolia, we formulated a dynamic energy scheduling strategy satisfying 24-h self-balancing constraints. Results indicate that a system producing 1415 tons of ammonia per day achieves a maximum hourly integrated profit of 69,838 CNY under optimal conditions: a hydrogen-to-nitrogen ratio of 2.98:1, operating pressure of 169 bar, reactor inlet temperature of 380 °C, and ammonia condensation temperature of −9 °C. Increasing the LAES throttle valve outlet pressure from 1 bar to 9 bar improved round-trip efficiency from 52.65% to 72.18%. The integrated-level parametric analysis reveals that the specific electricity consumption per unit mass of ammonia exhibits a non-monotonic trend with a minimum of 8.67 kWh/kg at −10 °C, reflecting the trade-off between refrigeration power consumption and cold energy recovery. In dynamic scheduling scenarios, the system maintains a maximum constant load of 45.78 MW with a steady-state liquid ammonia output of 6543 kg/h. This work optimizes both economic performance and system stability, providing a significant reference for the large-scale development of green ammonia systems.

10.46390/j.smensuen.29126.467.abstract: The Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) method has become, in the last decade, one of the most promising methods for obtaining and optimizing platinum-based electrocatalysts (Pt) for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), due to the atomic-level control over charge, dispersion and nanometer architecture. This review synthesizes the fundamentals of ALD deposition for obtaining Pt and Pt-alloy catalysts, from growth mechanisms and nucleation, precursor selection and the role of process conditions (surface chemistry, temperature, number of cycles) to their impact on the active structure and composition. Design strategies for ultra-low Pt charge catalysts, including advanced carbon support and conductive oxide depositions, as well as core-shell or Pt-skin approaches to optimize the use of the noble metal, are discussed. The paper analyzes how catalyst structure influences performance in the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), highlighting how particle size, spatial distribution, degree of alloying, and lattice voltages influence mass and specific activity. Finally, limitations, current gaps, and future directions are identified, including process scaling and standardization of test protocols, to accelerate the transition of laboratory ALD catalysts to commercial PEMFC applications.

10.54254/2755-2721/2026.ad33318.abstract: Ammonia, as a carbon-free and hydrogen-rich compound, with its high volumetric hydrogen density, mild liquefaction and storage transportation conditions, as well as a mature global supply chain, is gradually becoming an ideal hydrogen carrier. This article systematically reviews the research progress of the entire "ammonia-hydrogen" industrial chain. Firstly, this paper analyzes the high carbon emissions and low flexibility challenges faced by the traditional Haber-Bosch process in the energy transition, and discusses the design principles and performance bottlenecks of emerging green ammonia synthesis technologies such as the green Haber process, electrochemical nitrogen reduction, photocatalysis, and plasma catalysis. Secondly, the focus is placed on the diversified utilization of ammonia in the downstream conversion field. The technical paths, electrochemical performances and commercialization obstacles of direct ammonia solid oxide fuel cells, direct ammonia anion exchange membrane fuel cells and proton-conducting ceramic fuel cells are compared. Subsequently, based on this, an analysis from the perspectives of economy and environmental impact is conducted. Finally, the economic advantages of ammonia in the storage and transportation process, as well as its compatibility with existing infrastructure, give it the potential to replace traditional fuels in high-emission sectors such as shipping and power generation.

wx:__biz=MzAwOTExNzg4Nw==&mid=2657942885.abstract: 中国科学院大连化学物理研究所陈萍、郭建平研究团队与厦门大学吴安安副教授合作，发现氢化锂（LiH）是探索这一科学问题的理想模型体系。 注：文末有研究团队简介及本文科研思路分析 氨是化肥和几乎所有含氮化学品的氮源，其温和条件下的高效合成是化学科学长期追求的目标。Haber-Bosch合成氨被誉为20世纪最伟大的发明之一，但是需在高温高压（>400 °C，>100 bar）下运行，能耗与碳排放巨大。这是因为热催化过程中氮气活化和中间体加氢存在无法规避的矛盾，即标度关系（scaling relation）的制约：催化剂若能有效活化惰性的N≡N键，则对含氮中间体的吸附也会很强，这将阻碍后续加氢放氨过程；反之，若催化剂有利于产物脱附，则氮气活化能力不足。这一矛盾使得温和条件下高效合成氨极为困难，也是催化科学研究中的核心挑战。 光化学为解决这一科学问题提供了新的契机：不同波长的光子能量不同，理论上可以选择性地驱动特定的反应步骤，从而破解标度关系的制约。然而，在常规多相光催化体系中，表面关键中间体通常丰度低、寿命短，难以研究其特异性的光响应行为。中国科学院大连化学物理研究所陈萍、郭建平研究团队与厦门大学吴安安副教授合作，发现氢化锂（LiH）是探索这一科学问题的理想模型体系。区别于常规光催化体系，LiH在固氮产氨过程中生成可检测的稳定中间体（LiH1-x、Li2NH、LiNH2）；更为关键的是，这些中间体对不同波长的光呈现出截然不同的响应，为分步精准光调控反应提供了基础。基于这一特性，团队提出步骤特异性光激发策略，实现合成氨反应路径的解耦：即紫外光驱动氮气在LiH上还原生成含氮中间体，随后紫外光及可见光共同驱动含氮物种的加氢成氨。该策略从根本上绕过了标度关系制约，在常压、644 K条件下，该体系产氨浓度可以达到0.25%，突破该条件下热力学平衡所决定的极限浓度（0.13%）。 本工作首次提出了“分步光激发”策略：利用不同波长的光，分别驱动氮气固定和中间体加氢这两个在热催化中相互制约的步骤，为改变传统催化的标度关系瓶颈提供了新思路。这一成果不仅为温和条件下人工固氮提供了全新思路，该调控策略也有望拓展应用于甲烷活化、CO2还原等重要化学反应。 相关工作于近日发表在《美国化学会志》（Journal of the American Chemical Society）上，该工作的第一作者是中国科学院大连化学物理研究所关业勤副研究员和厦门大学博士研究生黄兆基。 原文（扫描或长按二维码，识别后直达原文页面）： Wavelength-dependent nitrogen fixation and hydrogenation to ammonia over lithium hydride catalyst Yeqin Guan, Zhaoji Huang, Kai Ma, Xiangdong Zeng, Kaixun Cui, Peng Zhang, Zibo Cheng, Muyao Liu, Junwang Tang, Anan Wu*, Jianping Guo*, Ping Chen* J.
